newsitem.title: UK: Bass to spend 670 million, create 7,000 jobs.
newsitem.headline: Bass to spend 670 million, create 7,000 jobs.

text.p: Sir Ian Prosser, chairman of British brewer-to-leisure group Bass Plc, said on Wednesday the company planned to spend 670 million pounds on the business during the year to September 30, 1997, creating some 7,000 jobs.

He said the company expected "continued buoyancy in UK consumer spending over the next year," and that the company's pubs and restaurants would "take advantage of this healthy background." His remarks were attached to Bass's full year 1996 results which showed a 12 percent increase in pre-tax profits to 671 million pounds.

The company plans a 300 million pound ($500.4 million) investment programme next year on its Bass Taverns, converting many pubs to branded concepts like All Bar One or Irish pubs O'Neills and refurbishing community pubs. This year the company invested, net of disposals, 568 million pounds in capital projects, which it calculates created at least 6,000 new jobs.

The company's Holiday Inns increased trading profit by 18.9 percent to 195 million, while its Bass Taverns' managed pubs grew operating profit by 22.8 percent to 221 million and its brewery business improved profits nine percent to 157 million. Its Britvic soft drinks division grew profits 8.7 percent to 50 million.
"Looking forward the hotel market dynamics continue to offer good prospects with growth in demand in the United States still forecast to exceed the growth in supply," said Prosser.

But the leisure division, which includes traditional Gala bingo halls and Corals betting shops, continued to be affected by the introduction of the national lottery and scratchcards. Profits were down 10.8 percent at 66 million.

Coral was hit by a remarkable one-off cost of 4.0 million pounds on the last Saturday of the financial year when all seven races at Ascot were won by the same jockey. A final dividend payout of 17.3 pence was recommended, making a total 25p for the year. ($1=.5995 Pound)
